sentences.text:
Criminal Revision No.2022/2014
28.07.2015
 Shri Surendra Singh, Sr. Advocate with Shri Priyankush
Jain, Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri S.S.Bisen, Advocate for the respondent.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

By this Criminal Revision under Section 397/401 of Cr.P.C. the applicant has challenged the order dated 16.7.2014 passed by the JMFC, Jabalpur in Criminal Appeal No.2857/1997 whereby the charges of offence under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) and 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (hereinafter referred to PF Act) have been framed due to violation of Rules 32(E), 42(H)
and 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules (for short PF Rules).
The brief facts of the case are that the respondent was the Food Inspector at the relevant time and went along with his force to the hotel of the applicant, which was prosecuting in the name of Nav Aathithya.
On 23.8.1990 he found that the Manager of the hotel was present and some spices were added in various vegetables and edibles prepared in the restaurant for the consumers.

The Food Inspector wanted to take the sample of the chilli power, which was kept in a polythene packet in the restaurant and thereafter purchased three packets of chilli power having 200 grams of chilli power in each packet.
On that packet it was mentioned that chilli power was manufactured by Popular Industries, Miloniganj, Jabalpur-accused No.3.
After taking steps for taking the sample, the sample was sent to the Public Analyst and the same was found appropriate.
Thereafter the sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory and nothing wrong was found in the sample.

However, it was found that the applicant had violated the Rules 32(E), 42(H) and 50 of the PF Rules, and therefore a complaint was filed for prosecution of the applicant for the offence under Section 7 read with Section 16 of the PF Act.

After considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, specially the pleading as made in para 4 of the complaint, it would be apparent that the packets of the chilli powder were kept in the restaurant for their use in making various edibles preparation.
It was not kept for sale.

It is alleged in the pleading that on request of the Food Inspector, one Manish Kumar Swami sold three packets of chilli to the Food Inspector so that the samples can be analized and to examine as to whether the chilli power was adulterated or not.
The applicant Rajwardhan Singhai was the owner of the restaurant, who did not sell anything to the Food Inspector.
According to pleading of para 4 in the complaint, the workers of the restaurant were adding chilli power in various edibles.
Hence it cannot be presumed that the chilli power kept in the restaurant was for sale.

If the Manager of that restaurant had sold any chilli Rajwardhan Singhai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 July, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152597834/
1 power, then it cannot be said that the applicant kept chilli power in the restaurant for sale, and therefore he was not required to follow such rules, which are required to be followed by the vendor or manufacturer.

sentences.text: The applicant cannot be held liable for violation of Rules 32(E), 42(H) and 50 of the PF Rules.

The learned senior counsel for the applicant has submitted that according to the reports given by the Public Analyst and the Central Food Laboratory, no edible oil was found added in the chilli power,
and therefore even to a manufacturer was not required to append any label as prescribed in Rule 42(H) of the PF Rules, and therefore even there is no violation of Rule 42(H) of the PF Rules had been done by the vendor or manufacturer of the sample of the chilli power.
On the basis of the aforesaid discussion, the chilli power was purchased by the workers of the applicant for its consumption in the restaurant.
It was not kept for their sale, and therefore it cannot be said that the applicant Rajwardhan Singhai has violated the Rules 32(E), 42(H) or 50 of the PF Rules.
It was not expected from the Food Inspector to take action against a person, who was prosecuting his business of the restaurant when the sample was found appropriate.

Actually the applicant was consumer of that chilli power and his servants were preparing edibles by adding chilli power purchased from the accused No.2 Kanhaiyalal and the chilli power was manufactured by the Popular Industries Miloniganj, Jabalpur.
Hence if the sample was found upto the mark, then no action was required against the applicant, who was not at all vendor of that sample.

If the Food Inspector has obtained the sample of the chilli power kept in the restaurant for its use to prepare edible for consumers, then by such an act, it cannot be said that the applicant was selling such chilli power to the public in general.
Under such circumstances, the trial Court has committed a manifest error in framing such charges against the applicant.
No alleged charge could be framed against the applicant, because he was not vendor of the chilli power.
Under such circumstances, the order dated 16.7.2014 passed by the JMFC Jabalpur against the applicant Rajwardhan Singhai is hereby set aside.
The applicant is discharged from the charge of Section 16(1)(a)(i) and 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act due to violation of Rules 32(E), 42(H) or 50 of the PF Rules.
The complaint filed by the respondent against the applicant is hereby dismissed with cost of Rs.500/- and that cost would be paid by the respondent person.

If the cost is deposited by the State,
then it can be recovered from the respondent-Food Inspector.
Certified copy as per rules.
